diff --git a/docs/handoff/DECISIONS.md b/docs/handoff/DECISIONS.md
index 6fe4443..5d67fd9 100644
--- a/docs/handoff/DECISIONS.md
+++ b/docs/handoff/DECISIONS.md
@@ -69,3 +69,4 @@ Backfilled 2026-11-03 from `docs/grammar.md#decided`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `docs/n
 | D63 | #806 may emit a private native scalar-return clone for an internal direct call returning exactly two ints whose result is immediately unpacked and cannot escape. Explicitly prove callee tuple construction/copy/return/cleanup and caller field-only consumption; route uncertain or escaping uses, task thunks and ordinary boxed calls through the existing function. Keep IR types and all runtime, binding and task ABIs unchanged; preserve lowered evaluation, exception tests, call-depth checks and cleanup | native.md explicitly reserves unboxing without IR type changes; #806 authorizes this narrow experiment. A private implementation clone is reversible and exposes no tuple layout across the runtime or interop boundary; mixed eligible and boxed call sites remain valid | general tuple scalar replacement; broad escape analysis; changing external ABI; removing checks for benchmark gains | [default] | Mill Board #806 authorized scope; D2, D7, D11, D15, D16, D23, D25, D30; native.md choices (2026-11-08) |
 | D64 | #807 may fuse only two adjacent same-block native string-concat assignments whose unnamed intermediate has one consuming concat use plus cleanup, when the third operand is an already live, immutable string parameter never reassigned, released or forgotten before the pair; leave all intervening evaluation, checks, calls, allocations, control flow, shared-use and uncertain shapes on the original path. A narrow audited runtime helper borrows three live strings, checks prefix then total byte length, copies each UTF-8 operand once into one exact-capacity buffer, and returns one ordinary owned string; preserve existing fatal capacity/allocation policy and cleanup, with no new exception or interop ABI | #807 explicitly authorizes allocation elimination; prepared-operand adjacency prevents moving any observable work or operand failure ahead of a prefix failure. Allocation count, exhaustion threshold and allocator-request-size text necessarily depend on the optimized allocation, as in D63; do not claim identical resource failure points or diagnose a simulated prefix OOM by length alone | evaluating arbitrary later operands before the original prefix; new OOM/exception policy; arbitrary reassociation; broad escape analysis; general unsafe infrastructure | [default] | Mill Board #807 authorized scope; D9, D11, D14, D23, D27, D30, D63; native.md string ownership/fault contracts; lower/vars.rs definitely-bound parameter reads (2026-11-08) |
 | D65 | #810 may specialize existing ordinary `pt_seq_get`/`pt_list_set` dispatch only when the immutable compiler-emitted descriptor is exactly `li` (`list[int]`): skip integer slot-descriptor traversal and element ownership/marking work, preserving the same `Slot` get/replace borrow and synchronization checks, negative/bounds checks, status paths and all other-descriptor fallbacks. Keep layout, codegen/runtime/binding/task ABIs, evaluation/fault order, loop holds and element-count elision unchanged | exact descriptor equality proves homogeneous integer slots without a new ABI or unsafe access; integers own and reach no heap value. This reversible pilot is retained only with repeatable same-host evidence beyond noise and no material regressions | unchecked raw access; lock/scheduler changes; widening to other descriptors; new typed runtime ABI; reopening D29 C | [default] | Mill Board #810 authorized dispatch-specialization scope and measurement gate; D2, D5, D11, D25, D27, D29, D30; seq.rs descriptor/ownership contract; sync::Slot get/replace (2026-11-08) |
+| D66 | #815 may add internal compiler/runtime entrypoints `pt_int_list_get` and `pt_int_list_set`, selected only for ordinary unheld accesses whose lowered receiver is proven exactly `list[int]`. They use the existing `Slot::get`/`replace` with empty element retain/store callbacks, preserving its synchronization/conflict and negative/bounds checks, read status overwrite, store failure status, pending-fault and evaluation/cleanup order. Keep generic and float dispatch, held-loop paths, representation, ownership, binding/task ABIs and D29 C unchanged; retain production only after repeatable same-host gains beyond noise and no material control regression | #815 expressly authorizes compiler selection after the rejected #810 shared-dispatch pilot; private typed calls avoid adding a branch to general/float accesses. This adds an internal compiler/runtime interface, not a language or externally supported binding interface; integer elements own or reach no heap values | repeating #810's rejected descriptor branch; raw unchecked access; changing `Slot`, holds, scheduler, external ABI or language; widening selection beyond proven integer lists | [default] | Mill Board #815 authorized scope and acceptance gates; D2, D5, D11, D25, D27, D29, D30; codegen/seq.rs typed operands; seq.rs and sync::Slot contracts (2026-11-09) |
